full_input_metadata.lineage: Official GNPS2 named library download, pinned by recorded SHA256. Not the repository-committed snapshot used by campaign147; no equality to the unavailable old GNPS host is asserted.

eligible_outputs: Identifiers for all input spectra plus all five terminal ranked-match branches; full matrices and processed objects are computational intermediates, not separately required outputs. Source coverage review and operation ledger retained.

source_coverage_review.rationale: Audited every source operation in the ledger against the final endpoint set. All six per-query analytical branches of the tutorial are required outputs: CosineGreedy query-5 unrestricted top-10 (call-172-15) and min_match>=5 (call-187-17); ModifiedCosine queries 5 (call-209-17), 11 (call-236-17) and 97 (call-258-17); plus the identifiers projection of the processed library (metadata chain call-83..91, peak chain call-107..109, parsing call-38). The two matching-matrix computations (CosineGreedy call-160, ModifiedCosine call-206) directly feed the required match lists and are exercised by the reference, oracle and independent solution. The CosineGreedy tables and modified query-5/11 tables that the trial termination did not serialize were recovered via the permitted endpoint-recovery route (unchanged invocations, same input, pinned stack) and cross-checked against the surviving recorded artifacts (best_matches_spectrum_97.csv row-for-row; identifiers CSV row-for-row; 30 npz matrix rows at both orientations; matrix-derived top-10 selection with tie analysis). Excluded branches have source-backed non-scientific roles: metadata tallies and heads (diagnostics), peaks-per-spectrum histograms (pipeline diagnostics), score-matrix corner prints (inspection), heatmaps (visual rendering of the matrix whose per-query scientific content is preserved in the required match tables), np.where(precursor_mz>600) (case-selection diagnostic; the spectrums[97] case is fixed in the task), RDKit structure drawings (rendering of the already-tabulated match lists), and the source's own json/pickle serialization of the processed library (representation of an intermediate whose identifier columns are exactly Output 1 and whose peaks fully determine the required scores; recoverable from the supplied input via public Steps 1-3). The all-pairs matrices are preparatory intermediates whose per-query terminal content the match tables preserve; the npz is retained reference-side as cross-validation evidence and does not supply any requested answer to the solver. No eligible terminal scientific result is omitted.
remaining_validation: Cross-stack (different OS/BLAS) determinism of scores within the 1e-12 tolerance is not separately demonstrated; honestly disclosed as a limitation in the grader rationale and not a claim made by the public contract

Rank-9/10 tie boundary: no equal scores exist in the current reference tables, so the tie tolerance is untested against real ties, but it is sound by construction because per-index value checks still bind every listed spectrum

solver_trajectory_audit: Recorded tools inspect supplied MGF and installed matchms sources, implement metadata/peak processing and per-query pairwise similarity computations, and write all six CSVs. No recorded retrieval/copy of reference answers. This is a trajectory audit, not proof against arbitrary covert behavior.
limits: All authoring and solver workers use GLM-5.3; independent programs share the matchms engine.
1e-12 score tolerance is supported by executed pinned-stack checks, not universal cross-engine portability.
No relevant top-k boundary ties were observed; tie-boundary selection portability is not established.
The public question has a duplicated Acceptance rules heading; retained unchanged in the tested bundle.
